question.leadin: Name these people who all formulated their own law codes.
question.text: This Athenian created Athens' first constitution, whose harshness gave rise to a word meaning "marked by extreme severity or cruelty."
question.clue: This man was given jurisdiction after Cylon tried to seize power, and the orator Demades joked that this man wrote in blood rather than in ink.

swap.leadin: Xerxes burned this city during his invasion of the Greek peninsula.
swap.text: Name this democratic city-state whose rulers included Solon, and whose Acropolis contains the Parthenon.
swap.clue: A bema, or speaker's platform, lies on this city's Pnyx hill.

question.leadin: In 336 BCE, this man succeeded his father, Philip II; within two years, he had pacified Greece and started an invasion of Persia.
question.text: Name this "Great" Macedonian leader, whose Hellenistic empire eventually stretched to India before he died at the age of 32.
question.clue: This husband of Roxana of Bactria fell ill after campaigning against the Paurava Dynasty of King Porus.

swap.leadin: Give the following about the aftermath of the 405 BCE Battle of Aegospotami [ay- gus-pah-tuh-mee].
swap.text: At Aegospotami, Lysander led a rout of the Athenian navy, thus essentially ending this war over control of the Greek mainland.
swap.clue: A history of this conflict records emissaries saying "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must" before killing and enslaving the population of Melos.

question.leadin: Answer the following about bees in Ancient Greece.
question.text: This culture's Treasury of Atreus is one of their beehive-shaped tombs called a tholos. This mainland Greek culture of the Bronze Age used Linear B script and made the Mask of Agamemnon.
question.clue: This culture originated the title potnia given to its great mother goddess, constructed huge beehive-shaped tombs called tholoi, and used the Linear B writing system.

swap.leadin: Texts with this title have been written by Tacitus and Polybius.
swap.text: Name this common title, which most famously refers to a book written by Herodotus of Helicarnassus.
swap.clue: A 40-volume work with this title discusses the goddess of Luck, Tyche, as well as the Roman constitution.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about an ancient battle.
question.text: The Persian Wars began because Athens and several other Greek cities supported the revolts in Asia Minor named after this region, which, along with other regions, including Dorus and Caria, was unsatisfied with its tyrants.
question.clue: The losing side in this conflict was defeated at Lade and supported by Athens, an alliance that prompted the Battle of Marathon when Darius I sent a punitive expedition.

swap.text: This Greek city on an isthmus had an ancient greased track called the diolkos replaced with a canal in the 19th century.
swap.clue: Lucius Mummius defeated the Achaean League in a battle near this city and razed it to the ground in 146 BCE. Thousands of hetaira prostitutes inhabited temples in this city, which was the first to develop black-figure pottery.

question.leadin: Their ranks included the Messenians, and they were subject to raids and surveillance by the Krypteia.
question.text: Identify these people who launched a rebellion following a 464 BCE earthquake.
question.clue: These people were the target of an annual declaration of war by elected Ephors, who would pardon their killers from miasma.

swap.leadin: Give these terms from ancient Greece.
swap.text: This eight-row formation of hoplites was a common unit of Greek troop deployment.
swap.clue: Two successive political parties with this name were merged with the Councils of the National-Syndicalist Offensive and the Carlist Party respectively.

question.leadin: Name these participants in acts of mass slaughter.
question.text: In 415 BC, Athens killed all the men of this neutral island city-state. Thucydides composed a noted debate in which the Athenians try to talk the city into surrendering.
question.clue: This island was involved in a diplomatic dispute immediately after the first battle of Mantinea, whose resolution likely inspired Euripides to write The Trojan Women.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the early Dark Ages.
swap.text: Historians look at the "migration" of people known by this term, which included the Huns and Ostrogoths. The Romans used this term to refer to the "uncivilized" tribes of people living outside their borders.
swap.clue: A word that is probably derived from the Greek word rha plus the Greek root of this word is traditionally used by stage actors to imitate the sound of indistinct conversation.

question.leadin: An independent state was established on this island in 1898, and lasted until 1913.
question.text: Name this island, home to the Minoan palace complex of Knossos.
question.clue: Modern archaeologists no longer agree that a civilization on this island collapsed after an eruption of Thera.

swap.text: Donald Kagan said that the surrender at Sphacteria "shook the world" in a history of this conflict. Thucydides also documented this conflict.
swap.clue: Donald Kagan wrote a celebrated history about a war of this name, in which the capture of Pylos caused one side to strand a contingent of troops on Sphacteria.

question.leadin: The Ptolemaic, Seleucid, and Antigonid dynasties all arose during this era.
question.text: Name this term from classical history for the era in which Greek culture flourished across Eurasia and Africa in the wake of Alexander the Great's conquests.
question.clue: Another sculpture from this period was attributed by Pliny the Elder to Athanodoros, Hagesandros, and Polydoros of Rhodes, although he inaccurately claims that it was made from one block of marble.

swap.leadin: This unit fought at the extreme left wing of the victorious side at the Battle of Leuctra.
swap.text: Name this elite fighting whose members are commemorate by a stone lion at the site of their destruction during the Battle of Chaeronea. It was composed of 150 pairs of lovers.
swap.answerHtml: Sacred Band of Thebes [or Hieros Lokhos; do not accept answers with “Carthage” since that’s a completely different group]
swap.clue: This group played a major role in winning a decisive victory at the Battle of Leuctra.

question.leadin: Identify these battles involving Thebes FTPE.
question.text: This 362 BCE battle saw the death of Epaminondas as the Thebans were defeated by a coalition consisting of Athens and Sparta. This battle ended Theban hegemony in Greece.
question.clue: At a 418 BC battle at this site, Sparta avenged its defeat at Sphacteria by overcoming an Argos-led alliance of democratic states.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about the so-called "Athenian Empire,"
swap.text: The "Athenian Empire" mainly grew out of the possessions of a "League" centered on this Aegean island. The 454 B.C. transfer of the League's treasury from this island to Athens symbolized Athens' growing imperialism.
swap.clue: Dying in this location was prohibited in a ritual purification during the Peloponnesian War.

question.leadin: The second ruler of this name commissioned the ship Syracusia.
question.text: Give this name of two rulers of Syracuse, the first of whom defeated the Etruscans at the Battle of Cumae, and the second of whom patronised Archimedes.

swap.text: This man had a hero cult at Athens because in mythology, he bestowed a boon on Athens when he died there under the hospitality of Theseus. He was raised by Polybus and Merope.
